Mrs Helen Cooper
Mrs Cooper is delighted to be executive headteacher at Sapperton which is a small, caring and successful school. She has worked in education for the past 28 years. She believes education is about nurturing confidence and recognising individual strengths in every child. Her goal is always to ensure that each child has the support they need to succeed and feel valued. In her leadership role, she is committed to building strong relationships. She understands that collaboration with parents, teachers, and the local community is key to providing the best possible experiences for the children.

Art and Design
At Sapperton, our intent for art is inspired by our vision to nurture faith; to inspire success. We believe that art is a vital part of every child’s education, fostering creativity, self-expression, and emotional development. Our art curriculum is designed to inspire and challenge pupils, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to experiment, invent, and create their own works of art, craft, and design. We nurture each child's natural curiosity and imagination through engaging, meaningful lessons that celebrate diverse artists, cultures, and techniques. Through exploring different media and processes, children develop confidence in their creative abilities and a deeper appreciation of visual art in the world around them. We place high value on using our beautiful natural surroundings as both a source of inspiration and a practical resource—whether sketching from nature, creating land art, or exploring natural textures and colours.
By the end of Key Stage 2, pupils will have a secure foundation in artistic vocabulary, a growing awareness of visual elements such as colour, pattern, texture, and composition, and the confidence to reflect on and evaluate their own and others' work. We ensure that pupils not only develop their artistic techniques, such as drawing, painting, sculpture, and digital media, but also learn how to think critically about art. Ultimately, we strive to cultivate a lifelong enjoyment of the arts and encourage children to see themselves as artists in their own right, feeling successful with their own creations.

Remembering Together in Maple Class
Maple Class have been learning about poppies and discussing why we wear them to remember those who have served and sacrificed in wars. The children shared their thoughts about remembrance and why it is important that we remember others. To mark this special time, everyone contributed to create a beautiful collaborative poppy wreath. Each child's poppy helped to make something special that we can share together as a class, reminding us of the importance of remembering.

Court Is in Session! ⚖️
For our final lesson of our RE unit, Creation or Science: Conflicting or Complimentary?, we transformed our classroom into a courtroom to explore the big question: Do science and religious beliefs conflict, or can they complement one another?
The class took on the roles of the prosecution, defence and jury. Working in their teams, they gathered evidence, prepared their arguments and presented their cases. The jury listened carefully to both sides before considering the evidence and reaching their verdict.
It was fantastic to see everyone putting their learning into practice, thinking critically and respectfully considering different viewpoints. The courtroom debate encouraged us to question, reason and explore how science and religious beliefs can sometimes challenge one another, but may also offer different ways of understanding the world.
A brilliant way to conclude our unit, showcasing teamwork, thoughtful discussion and some very persuasive arguments! Well done, everyone! ⚖️👏

The children in Reception have been learning about Raksha Bandhan, a Hindu festival that celebrates the special bond between brothers and sisters, as well as love, care and protection within families.As part of their learning, each child made a rakhi bracelet. Traditionally, a rakhi is tied around a family member’s wrist as a symbol of love, care and the promise to look after one another.

Mrs Meg Crampton
Mrs Crampton joined Sapperton in 2023, bringing over 15 years of teaching experience across Gloucestershire and having achieved a National Professional Qualification in Headship. She is passionate about teaching a broad range of subjects, particularly English, maths, history and languages, and enjoys creating a positive, community-focused school environment.
Alongside her role as Head of School, she remains dedicated to classroom teaching, implementing the latest educational research to develop independent and successful learners throughout the school. Building positive and trusting relationships within the Sapperton community is always a priority, as she believes that everyone should have the opportunity to flourish and succeed.

Maple
In Maple Class, curiosity grows, imaginations soar, and every day is an adventure! Year 1 and Year 2 continue their school journey here, guided by our fantastic teachers, Mrs Wenban and Mrs Trinder, and supported by our ever-enthusiastic teaching assistants, Mrs Maloney and Ms Jefferies. Together, we are a team ready to turn learning into something magical.
We have a beautiful space that enables us to provide our pupils with an exciting learning environment, incorporating independent discovery alongside teacher-led activities. We are also lucky enough to have a variety of outdoor areas for Maple Class, including a dedicated learning space in the playground, a mud kitchen, and a designated Forest School area.
In Maple Class, phonics and early reading are not just important; they are a daily adventure! Whether we are playing with sounds, exploring silly rhyming words, or diving into enchanting storybooks, children are surrounded by opportunities to fall in love with reading. With a sparkle of encouragement from our teachers, our young readers grow in confidence, devouring stories one page at a time.
Maths in Maple Class is never boring. It is hands-on, practical and packed with fun! Whether we are measuring mysterious treasures from our outdoor adventures or solving puzzles with our friends, maths becomes a part of our everyday play. Children count, build and problem-solve, all while having a blast and discovering that numbers are everywhere.
Our classroom is a happy, welcoming place where everyone is celebrated for who they are. We become scientists, artists, storytellers and outdoor explorers, with plenty of time to play and discover in our lovely school grounds. Each child's ideas and questions are welcomed, and our supportive staff are always ready with a smile and a helping hand.
Families are a big part of our Maple Class community. We love sharing our learning through regular updates, inviting grown-ups to join us for special events, and working together to ensure every child shines. There is always something exciting happening, and we cannot wait to welcome you into our wonderful classroom world.

Rowan Class Becoming Keen Historians
Rowan Class have been learning about the remarkable work of Lord Shaftesbury and the important changes he helped bring about during Victorian times. The children explored how he campaigned to improve the lives of poor and vulnerable people, including children working in factories and mines. They discovered how his efforts led to better working conditions, improved education opportunities, and greater protection for children. Rowan Class enjoyed discussing the lasting impact of these changes and reflecting on how they continue to influence society today.
